claims.statement: The domain layer has zero framework imports — no Gin, no GORM, no Redis, no asynq — only Go standard library and internal/pkg/clock.

Domain errors are constructed via helpers in errors.go (NewNotFoundError, NewValidationError, NewConflictError, etc.) and standardized by codes in error_codes.go, with the transport layer's response/ package being the only place that translates them to HTTP.

The wallet aggregate is a self-contained bounded context: its repository interfaces (WalletTopupRepository, WalletPaymentRepository, WalletIPNRepository) live in internal/domain/wallet/repository.go, not in the global ports directory.

Wallet payment state machine uses qmuntal/stateless with states pending, verified, authorised, completed, failed, reversed and triggers verify, reject, authorise, ipn_completed, ipn_failed, ipn_reversed; completed/failed/reversed are terminal.

Double-entry accounting rules in AccountingRules.ValidateTransactionGroup and ValidateBalancedTransaction enforce that the sum of debits equals the sum of credits for every ledger group, and are verified by property-based tests using gopter.

All business time goes through internal/pkg/clock (Now, NowUTC, TodayStart, TodayEnd, UnixNow) per ADR-006; admin clock endpoints are mounted only in non-prod builds, and the narrow time.Now() exceptions are limited to infrastructure measurements (event-bus duration, health-check response time).

Domain ports split into ports/infrastructure (audit, cache, disbursement, notification — implemented by infra adapters) and ports/services (ledger, loan, payroll, settlement, timesheet, transaction — application services compose these with ports).

Domain events are declared in events.go (50+ types) and produced by per-aggregate factories (event_factory_*.go); they are persisted in the same DB transaction as the state change and pushed to Redis Streams post-commit via the outbox pattern.
